blocks.text: Network architecture is the overall design of a computer network. It shows how computers, servers, and other devices are arranged (as shown in Figure 1.2). It also defines how data is transmitted across the network. Network architecture includes hardware, software, and communication rules. A good architecture helps the network work efficiently. It also supports future expansion of the network.

blocks.alt: An Internet cloud at the top is wired to a wireless router with Wi-Fi waves; from the router a branching cable runs down to a desktop computer, a laptop, a server rack, a tablet and a printer.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.2: Network architecture shows how devices and components are organized in a network (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.2).

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Provide pictures or names of devices. Students match device names with functions. Discuss answers

A network works by sending data from one device to another. Data is broken into small packets before transmission. These packets travel through cables or wireless signals. Networking devices guide packets to the correct destination. The receiving device reassembles the packets into the original data. This process allows smooth and fast communication.
